name: v24-scroll-reveal
change: Three below-the-fold sections ("Stand out, build trust, and...", "Branded Call performance analytics", "Secure Branding: Your Brand, Only on Verified Calls") start hidden (opacity:0; transform:translateY(40px)) and are revealed by a scroll-position-driven, rAF-animated inline script (scrollY threshold crossing starts a 2000ms requestAnimationFrame + performance.now() interpolation of opacity 0->1 / translateY 40px->0, writing inline style per frame, finalizing to a one-way latch) -- an IX2-style scroll-triggered reveal, deterministic by construction (rAF/performance.now are driven by matchy's page.clock virtual clock during capture; no Date/setTimeout/wall-clock dependence).
edit:
site/index.html: added ` data-scroll-reveal=""` attribute to the opening `
` tag of 3 existing sections (the 4th, 6th, and 8th of the page's 13 `section-zero` elements, 0-indexed 3/5/7 -- headings 'Stand out, build trust, and...', 'Branded Call performance analytics', 'Secure Branding: Your Brand, Only on Verified Calls'), plus one `
knockOnEffects: translateY(40px) is a transform (paint-only, does not affect box-model/layout flow), so no other element's position or the page's total height shifts because of the hidden starting state or the animation -- confirmed by the observed settle-on run producing zero visual_region_changed/layout-adjacent issues anywhere else on the page.

OBSERVED (full run, settle default-on, testbed/.runs/v24-scroll-reveal/diff-result.json, re-verified after the rAF redesign): status=pass, 0 issues, 0 warnings; both sides' bundles record determinism.settle="ran" and determinism.quiescence="reached" (no timeout) -- the deserved outcome. Full settle's quiescence loop keeps advancing the virtual clock (dwell/quiescence budget up to 5000ms) until no un-ignored mutations occur for its quiet window, which comfortably absorbs the 2000ms rAF animation (each per-frame inline-style write is itself a counted mutation) plus its settle-quiet window, so every reveal finishes and the end state (opacity 1, transform none) is what gets screenshotted.

RESOLVED (was FLAGGED in the initial scrollY-latch-only design; fixed by redesigning the reveal itself to be rAF-animated, per orchestrator direction -- fixture-builder did not choose the redesign, only implemented and re-verified it): the `--no-settle` negative control now demonstrably fails as intended. OBSERVED (manual run, /tmp/claude-1000/v24-nosettle/diff-result.json): status=warn, 10 issues total -- 3 `style_changed` (warning severity, property=opacity, from=0.485 to=1 -- a section frozen mid-animation at ~48.5% progress) + 7 `visual_region_changed` (info severity), 5 of which anchor by text to the three hidden sections and their sub-elements ('THE SOLUTION' eyebrow + 'Identify patterns in call outcomes...' bullet under the two reveal sections that also show style_changed; 'Display your brand only on verified calls' and 'Secure Branding: Your Brand, Only on Verified Calls' under the third), plus 2 unanchored region-level visual diffs. Both sides' no-settle bundles record determinism.settle="skipped", determinism.quiescence="notRun", determinism.lazyLoadPass="ran" (the legacy path) -- legacy's coarser scroll-through (~100ms dwell/step, 250ms at the end) crosses the scrollY reveal thresholds late enough in the pass that the 2000ms rAF animation is still mid-flight when the screenshot is taken, producing the observed partial-opacity/mid-transform diffs. This is the intended settle-earns-its-keep proof; not wired into CI, per instructions -- see expected-issues.json notes for the full breakdown.
